sections.heading: Flagged items in detail
paragraphs: CFO vs. Net Income Conversion: Operating cash flow converted -356% of reported net profit. Profit is running ahead of cash generation, which points to working-capital or accrual quality issues.
FCF Generation Consistency: Free cash flow was positive in 0 of the last 5 reported years. Repeated FCF deficits mean growth is being funded by the balance sheet rather than by the business.
Debt-to-Equity Trajectory: Leverage moved from 4.00x to 5.52x equity. Leverage is high enough to transmit an earnings shock directly into equity value.
Share Dilution Check: The share count changed +18.9% a year. Dilution transfers value from existing holders to new issuance.
ROE vs. ROCE Quality: Return on capital employed of 11.0% with ROE of 25.2% is close to or below the cost of capital, so growth destroys rather than creates value.
Interest Coverage Safety: Operating profit covers interest 2.0 times. Coverage is thin enough that a profit dip would pressure debt service.
Book Value Compounding: Book value per share compounded -0.8% annually. Retained earnings are not translating into balance-sheet growth.

Auditor & Governance Cleanliness: Aggregating the accounting evidence: 5 hard red flags and 2 watch items, with a LojikX™ Consistency Score of 83/100. The pattern of flags warrants a closer read of the auditor notes and related-party disclosures.
